layout: Portrait handwritten page filled nearly to its lower edge. Underlined heading, four-line opening paragraph with raised comme, a six-line left-braced data system (5), a quotient-construction paragraph with overwritten numerator and raised fermés, displayed functor (6) with an inserted I, final assertion with raised parenthesis and underline, a three-line diagonal lower-left NB note, bottom-right warning, and small pale author page 6 at lower left.

changes.evidence: An isolated dark point follows the final low e-stroke, above the title underline. The title is underlined across its full width.

The terminal letter has a tall upright and a short crossbar extending to the right, matching t rather than a rounded d. The preceding st, low an, looped d and ar strokes can be followed; retain the written final t and the underline.
The word ends at the short final i-stroke with its separate dot. A wide blank follows before constructivement; there is no terminal e. The d/f stems and low intervening sequence are visible.
The c/o and low joined m/m/e strokes form a separate short line above ci-dessus, after the system a) b) c) phrase. It is an added word at this position, not written on the main ci-dessus baseline.

changes.final: one left brace grouping a), b), c)
changes.evidence: A long left grouping stroke bends outward at the level of (5), then continues down beside b) and c) to a dark angular end. It groups the six main baselines; it is not an additional letter, relation or independent mathematical arrow.
The raised words sur S are linked by one curved connector to the gap after lisse and before partout. The small hook right of S continues into that connector; there is no separate comma there.
The sous- prefix and schém sequence are followed by a distinct point. No a/s letters occur between that point and the separate comma before de Y. The written abbreviation is preserved.
A separate curved comma occurs to the right of the abbreviation point, before de. The point and comma are two marks, not one blurred ending. Both witnesses omit the comma.

changes.place: L9 struck word after sur S
changes.evidence: A short word-sized patch is deliberately crossed by a thick horizontal stroke. Only low irregular bumps survive; every letter cannot be separated. Keep C’s tentative avec explicitly unsure rather than claim a recovered full word. Blind B04 adds et as a possible reading of the short upright and lower curve; the cancellation still prevents resolution.

The loop is small and open, with a long strongly extended lower-left stem and a short hooked upper end. This favors a phi-shaped written glyph; the slash/loop can also represent varnothing, so the alternative remains. Its role as the empty-set sign is unchanged.

The upper-left descending diagonal and short lower-right continuation of X survive. A heavily reinforced rising diagonal with a long lower-left stem forms the replacement Y, directly over that earlier letter. Record both states without moving the quotient slash or sigma.
The upper stroke of the relation is visibly wavy, with a rise and dip, while the lower stroke is straight. This is the written simeq, not a pair of straight equality bars.

After the low m there is an isolated point-like mark followed by a detached s. The point favors an abbreviation stop, yielding sous-schém.s, but a very reduced a remains possible. No unmarked expansion is supplied.

The capital I and its following comma occupy the added slot before sigma. A raised peaked connector curls down to the existing gap after tilde-A, distinguishing this insertion from the original tuple entries. The map itself has a left bar, one shaft and a right arrowhead.
A short straight underline lies immediately below the first NB only; the second NB has no underline. Both pairs of capitals are readable.
After ce foncteur, the next diagonal baseline starts with the low e/s strokes and a tall crossed t. There is no preceding n or apostrophe. The word is est, not n’est.

changes.place: Diagonal note, compatibility phrase and M0924
changes.evidence: Compatible has a rounded initial c/o, joined m/p strokes, a tall t and the following i/b/l/e sequence. Aux shows a low a/u sequence followed by a two-stroke x; this resolves M0924. Images has a dotted i and long g descender; inverses has dotted i, low n/v/e and the final r/s/e/s sequence. The words are present on this sheet.

The three marginal ellipsis dots follow the diagonal line of inverses around that label. Do not duplicate the label as note text or infer a continuation on another sheet.

The terminal sequence again has a low m, a point-like mark and a detached final s. Schém.s is the preferred literal reading, while schémas remains an explicit alternative because the point could be a reduced a.

changes.place: L19 final insertion relative to comma
changes.evidence: A separate baseline comma follows relatifs. The curved connector from the raised parenthesis ends in the gap after the final s and before that comma, placing (pour les iso) inside the comma boundary. The comma remains outside the inserted text.
A small pale 6, with an upper curved stem and closed lower bowl, appears at the lower-left sheet edge beneath the diagonal note. It is distinct from the large upright formula label (6).

doubts.reason: B04: thick horizontal ink covers the letter bodies. A low initial curve and short upright can also fit et, as the blind reader proposed. Neither complete reading is secure; preserve the canceled-word doubt.

doubts.reason: A small open loop has a strongly extended lower-left stem and a short hooked upper end. It is phi-like, but the handwritten slash/loop can also represent varnothing. It is used as the empty-set sign. The preferred glyph differs from C/H and is therefore also logged as a cropped reading change.

After the low m is a point-like mark followed by a detached final s. The point may be an abbreviation stop or a very reduced a. Both witnesses expand/read the full word; keep the visual alternative instead of silently choosing an expansion.

This occurrence again has a small isolated point-like mark before a detached final s. The ink does not certify whether it is an abbreviation stop or a reduced a. The whole word is included in the lower blind box.

notes: The page proposes a constructive definition of a courbe standart over a general base S from a proper smooth Y of relative dimension 1, two finite etale subschemes tilde-A and I, and a freely acting involution on tilde-A. It forms a quotient hat-X, identifies the image A, removes I to define X, and writes the functor (6). This is a summary of the transcription, not a proof or verification of those assertions.

The diagonal NB says that the functor is compatible with inverse images. The main text asserts full faithfulness for isomorphisms, but the author’s separate bottom-right note says faux tel quel !. Both the assertion and the author’s objection are retained; no correction of the mathematics is inserted into the text.

Standart and the ending défini are literal. The clear abbreviation sous-schém. in (5)b is followed by a separate comma. Two later plural-looking forms remain ambiguous between schém.s and schémas; their tiny point-like mark is not silently expanded. Dim and iso remain in their short forms.

The quotient numerator is visibly overwritten: the lower-right part of X survives beneath the reinforced Y. Both states are recorded at medium confidence. The relation A simeq tilde-A/sigma has a wavy upper stroke, unlike the two straight bars of equality.

The empty-set sign in (5)b has a small open loop and long descending stem; phi is the preferred visual alternative, with varnothing retained. This affects glyph identification, not the role of the sign in the statement. The long left grouping stroke of (5) is represented as a brace; its dark angular terminal is not treated as an independent content arrow.

Raised comme, sur S, fermés, tuple I, and (pour les isos) are all retained at their observed attachments. The final insertion comes before the baseline comma. The hook after sur S belongs to its connector and supplies no independent comma. The upright (6) belongs only to the displayed map; the diagonal NB note runs around it and is complete on this sheet as transcribed.

Line count 28 = 19 main baselines including the title, six baselines of (5), and (6); four raised verbal baselines (comme, sur S, fermés, pour les isos); three diagonal NB baselines; the bottom-right warning baseline; and the small page-number baseline. The overwritten Y and inserted I occupy existing formula baselines and are not counted again.

The original and both native halves, followed by all 11 saved evidence crops, were inspected once. No OCR, web lookup, TeX compilation, or independent mathematical check was used. Blind box B04 contains the whole of (5) and the overlapping comme/ci-dessus lead-in; B08 contains the complete lower functor passage and overlapping diagonal note so that no formula, marginal text or insertion is cut.

The preferred first alternatives phi, sous-schém.s and schém.s differ from the primary glyph/spelling in both witnesses. Each therefore has a medium-confidence reading-change row as well as a retained doubt; none changes the mathematical content. All handwritten numeric occurrences are in blind boxes: dimension 1 and label (5) in B04, label (6), the final reference (5), and small page number 6 in B08.

Independent audit: the small canceled word in (5)b now retains avec/et alternatives. Partout has the tall internal/final t strokes rather than the extra humps required by purement. The quotient retains the visible older X beneath the reinforced Y; the lower-right arm of X survives. The final inserted parenthesis has a separate terminal s in isos, unlike the baseline iso above. The shortened schém.s forms and phi/empty-set ambiguity remain. No independent mathematical check was performed.
